title: Structural MRI learning identifies Alzheimer-like patterns associated with cognition
summary: A support-vector classifier learned Alzheimer-like structural patterns after age adjustment and identified 8.8% of an additional Human Connectome Project Aging sample as structurally Alzheimer-like. Those patterns were associated with cognitive differences, with additional biomarker analyses in mild cognitive impairment. These are cross-sectional exploratory associations; they do not establish future Alzheimer conversion, a clinical diagnosis in asymptomatic people or screening benefit.
organization: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Massachusetts General Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations, exact primary front identity and current primary PubMed notice metadata; version dates distinguished.

evidence.tested: Age-detrended structural MRI classification, additional-cohort cognitive associations and MCI biomarker comparisons.
evidence.unknown: Longitudinal disease conversion, independent clinical screening performance and patient benefit remain unestablished; development-stage feature weighting can inflate internal classification.
evidence.ai_role: An RBF support-vector machine learns weighted, age-adjusted cortical/subcortical patterns and assigns Alzheimer-like structural scores.
